smeTaxExemption.subtitle: Youth 90% for 5 years; age 60+, disabled and career-break workers 70% for 3 years; up to ₩2M a year — eligibility, end date and tax saved in {year}

in.militaryHint: Active-duty soldier, regular reservist, auxiliary police or firefighter, social service agent, or active-duty officer/NCO. Up to 6 years ({cap} months) is subtracted from your age.

in.excluded: My company's industry is not an eligible industry
in.excludedHint: Hospitals and clinics, banks and insurers, legal, accounting and tax services, general cram schools, bars and cafés, and similar businesses do not qualify.

youth.label: Youth
youth.hint: Age 15–34 on the contract date (military service subtracted)

senior.label: Age 60+
senior.hint: Age 60 or older on the contract date

disabled.label: Disabled
disabled.hint: Registered disabled person, wounded national merit holder, 5·18 injured person, or Agent Orange patient with a disability grade

careerBreak.label: Career break
careerBreak.hint: Left a job held for 1+ year due to marriage, pregnancy, childbirth, childcare, children's education or family care, and returned to work 2 to under 15 years later

result.label: Tax saved in {year}
result.ok: You qualify for the {kind} {pct}% exemption. It applies to pay earned through {end}.
result.ended: You qualified for the {kind} {pct}% exemption, but the period ended on {end}.
result.later: You qualify for the {kind} {pct}% exemption. It starts on {first}.
result.no: You do not qualify for the exemption.
result.rateValue: {pct}% of income tax (up to ₩2M a year)
result.earnedCut: Reduction in earned income tax credit
result.pastNote: If you did not receive the exemption in past years, you can claim it back through a Hometax correction request within 5 years.
result.note: Tax includes the 10% local income tax. This estimate assumes no deductions other than social insurance and your own basic deduction, equal monthly pay and an unchanged salary. The earned income tax credit shrinks in proportion to the exemption (Enforcement Decree Art. 27(9)), so the tax saved can be less than the exemption itself.

reasons.early: The {kind} exemption applies only to people hired on or after {from}.
reasons.deadline: Current law covers only people hired by {deadline}. Proposals to extend the deadline are before the National Assembly.
reasons.young: You are {age} on the contract date, below the youth minimum age of 15.
reasons.old: You are {age} on the contract date and still {adj} after subtracting military service, above the youth maximum of 34. A contract signed by {until} would count as youth.
reasons.senior: You are {age} on the contract date, so you are not in the 60+ category.
reasons.industry: The exemption does not apply if your company's main business is not an eligible industry.

sim.title: If you change jobs or served in the military
sim.moved: The period continues from {first}, when you first received the exemption, and ends on {end}. Starting fresh from your current start date ({start}) would have meant {endIfNew}, but the law counts from the first start date regardless of job changes. Submit the application again to your new company.
sim.stay: If you move to another SME, the period does not restart: it continues from {first} and ends on {end}. If the new company is also an eligible SME, submit the application again and keep the exemption for the remaining period.
sim.army: You are {age} on the contract date, or {adj} after subtracting {military} months of military service. A contract signed by {until} counts as youth. Without subtracting service, the cutoff would be {untilNoMil}.
sim.armyNone: You are {age} on the contract date. A contract signed by {untilNoMil} counts as youth. Military service (up to 6 years) pushes this date back.
sim.armyOther: Categories other than youth have no upper age limit, so military service is not used.

industries.title: Eligible industries
industries.desc: The company must be an SME under the Framework Act on SMEs (including non-profits) whose main business is one of the industries below (Enforcement Decree of the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, Art. 27(3)). Central and local governments, public institutions and local public enterprises are excluded regardless of industry.
eligible: Electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply
Water supply, sewage, waste management and materials recovery
Accommodation and food services (excluding bars, cafés and other non-alcoholic beverage outlets)
Information and communication (excluding video viewing rooms and virtual asset trading/brokerage)
Market research and public opinion polling
Architectural, engineering and other scientific and technical services
Other professional, scientific and technical services (excluding veterinary)
Business facilities management, business support and rental services
Technical and vocational training institutes, computer academies
Repair of personal and household goods
Libraries, historical sites and similar recreation services
excluded: Finance and insurance (banks, insurers, securities firms, card companies)
Health care (hospitals, clinics, dentists, oriental medicine clinics)
Legal, accounting and tax services, management consulting
Schools and general cram, tutoring and language academies (technical/vocational and computer academies qualify)
Bars, cafés and other non-alcoholic beverage outlets
Amusement services such as PC rooms, karaoke and amusement parks
Other personal services such as beauty, laundry and funeral services

people.title: Who cannot receive it even at an eligible company
items: Executives (as defined in Art. 40(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Corporate Tax Act)
The company's largest shareholder or investor (the owner for sole proprietorships), their spouse, their lineal relatives (and spouses) and other relatives
Daily workers — contract and fixed-term workers are not excluded and can qualify if they meet the other requirements
People whose National Pension and employee health insurance contributions cannot be confirmed (unless they are not required to join)
People working for central or local governments, public institutions or local public enterprises (civil servants, public corporation staff, etc.)
People working for companies that are not SMEs (mid-sized or large companies)

apply.title: How to apply
items: Submit the SME employee income tax exemption application to your employer (the withholding agent) by the end of the month after the month you were hired. Youth applicants attach proof of military service.
Your employer can apply the exemption to withholding from the month after it receives your application, and files the list of exempt employees with the tax office by the 10th of that month.
If you change jobs, submit the application again to your new company. The period continues from your first start date.
If you missed a year, you can claim it back through a Hometax correction request within 5 years. If you have left the company, apply directly to the tax office for your address.
If you receive the exemption without meeting the requirements, you must repay 105% of the underpaid tax (Restriction of Special Taxation Act, Art. 30(5)).

reform.title: 2026 tax reform proposal (before the National Assembly, not reflected)
reform.text: The government's August 2026 tax reform proposal reportedly expands the exemption for SME employees outside the capital region (youth periods of up to 10 years depending on region, and up to 90% for age 60+, disabled and career-break workers) and extends the deadline. Nothing changes until the National Assembly passes it, so this calculator uses current law (hired by December 31, 2026; youth 90% for 5 years, others 70% for 3 years).

smeTaxExemption.source: Sources: Restriction of Special Taxation Act Art. 30 and its Enforcement Decree Art. 27 · laws in force as of November 2026. The final month counts the period from the start date inclusive.
